To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sub-cortical fauna of dead conifers is different between primeval and managed forest.
the beetle fauna of standing and fallen dead pines and Norway spruces in managed forests in Finland was more diverse and abundant, but less specific, than in primeval forests.
the sub-cortical Coleopteran beetle fauna of dead conifer trunk was richer and more abundant in a managed forest than in a primeval forest in central Finland.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of the sub-cortical Coleopteran fauna of conifer trunks.
the effects of forest management on the subcortical Coleoptera.
the effects of man-made forest management on the sub-cortical fauna of dead conifer truncks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the species composition of sub-cortical beetles in dead conifer trees is strongly affected by forest management.
the beetle fauna of dead trees is strongly affected by man's activities.
the beetle species composition in dead pines is not maintained in managed forests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beetle species richness in dead pines in the managed forests of central Finland is high, and that the proportion of rare species is also high in comparison with other studies in Finland.
the sub-cortical fauna of dead pines and/or spruces is not well conserved in managed forests.
the sub-cortical fauna in dead conifer trees is strongly affected by human activity, and that the fauna in managed forests is different from the one in primeval forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sub-cortical Coleopteran fauna of dead conifers is strongly affected by forest management.
the sub-cortical fauna of dead trees is not a good indicator of the species composition of the primeval forests in Finland.
there is a strong need for a better understanding of the ecology of these species in managed forests.
